title: Smooth markings, normalization of the twist, and its component degrees
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $f:X\to S$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]). Assume every geometric fibre $Y/\Omega$ is nonempty, reduced and pure of dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension], with at worst nodes: every nonsmooth closed point has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as an $\Omega$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Connectedness of the fibres is not required. Let $K$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] on $X$, supplied with identifications of its restriction to every geometric fibre $Y$ with the canonical adjunction line $K_{Y/\Omega}$ of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be pairwise disjoint sections in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with $n\geq0$. Their ideal product defines an effective Cartier divisor $D=\sum_i a_i(S)$, a finite disjoint union of copies of $S$ and hence a relative effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. Put $L=K\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)$, using [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. It is invertible. For every $S'\to S$, the pullback of $D$ is the corresponding divisor of the pulled-back sections and $L_{S'}\simeq K_{S'}\otimes\mathcal O_{X_{S'}}(D_{S'})$ canonically [def-pc-module-pullback]. These comparisons preserve tensor products of sections, commute with composition, and are natural under isomorphisms of families carrying the given $K$ and the markings to one another.
For a geometric fibre $Y/\Omega$, a reduced irreducible component $Z$, and its normalization $\nu:C\to Z\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], $C$ is a proper smooth connected curve. Let $B_C$ be its reduced divisor of ambient nodal branches, counting both branches at a self-node, and $M_C$ the reduced points above the markings lying on $Z$. The supports of $B_C$ and $M_C$ are disjoint and consist of $\Omega$-rational points; each marking occurs once. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\nu^*(L|_Y)\simeq\Omega^1_{C/\Omega}\otimes\mathcal O_C(B_C+M_C),$$
and
$$\deg\nu^*(L|_Y)=2g(C)-2+\#B_C+\#M_C.$$
Here $g(C)=\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-sc-genus], differentials are [def-sc-kahler-differentials], and degree means $\chi(C,F)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ for an invertible module $F$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. This agrees with divisor degree on $C$. For $n=0$, $D$ and $M_C$ are empty. The lemma constructs no $K$, asserts no positivity, and imposes no stability, modification map, or smooth generic fibre.

proof.text: Properness includes separatedness. By [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], each $a_i$ is a closed immersion in $X$. Let $U$ be the relative smooth locus. By [lem-trf-geometric-pure-fibre-point-dimension], applied to the finitely presented $f$ whose nonempty geometric fibres are pure of dimension one, $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})=1$ for every $x\in X$; so $U/S$ is smooth of relative dimension one in the fibrewise meaning of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Each $a_i(S)$ is still closed in $U$ and is isomorphic to $S$. Its map to $S$ is finite locally free of rank one: on a base affine the algebra is $A$, free on $1$. Implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] makes it a relative effective Cartier divisor on $U/S$. Its ideal is generated by $1$ off its image, so the same Cartier property holds on $X$. No properness of $U/S$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0B9D, lemma-divisors-on-curves, (1) implies (2); divisors.tex Tag 067R, lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion

proof.text: Put $I=\prod_i I_i$, where $I_i$ is the ideal of $a_i(S)$. Near any point at most one marking is present: remove the other finitely many closed images. Thus $I$ there equals that marking ideal, or the unit ideal if none is present. Its local generator is therefore a non-zero-divisor. The closed subscheme defined by $I$ is the disjoint union of the $a_i(S)$, since these descriptions cover $X$; equivalently the pairwise comaximal ideals have product equal to intersection. Over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ this union has algebra $A^n$, free as an $A$-module, hence is finite and flat over $S$. It is consequently a relative effective Cartier divisor by [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. Its associated line [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] is invertible, and so is $L=K\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)$ by [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible]. For $n=0$ the ideal is $\mathcal O_X$ and the subscheme is empty.

For any $g:S'\to S$, apply [lem-pc-recd-pullback] to the given flat finitely presented $f$ and the relative divisor of step 2. It gives the relative divisor $D_{S'}$ and its line comparison. The disjoint-union description shows $D_{S'}$ is precisely the divisor of the pulled-back sections. The natural tensor comparison of [lem-pc-scheme-pullback-monoidal-existing] then gives $g_X^*L\simeq g_X^*K\otimes\mathcal O_{X_{S'}}(D_{S'})$. Here $K_{S'}$ denotes $g_X^*K$; no construction or base-change theorem for a relative dualizing line is needed.

The comparisons of step 3 are the local ones sending a frame $t^{-1}$ of $\mathcal O(D)$, dual to a Cartier ideal generator $t$, to the frame $(g_X^\sharp t)^{-1}$ of the pullback divisor line. If $t$ is replaced by $ut$, the inverse frame changes by $u^{-1}$ on both sides, so these maps glue. In local frames of $K$ they take tensor products of sections to the tensor products of their images. For two successive base changes the image of $t$ is obtained by composing the two ring maps; thus both routes send $t^{-1}$ and every local frame of $K$ to the same frames. Their equality proves composition compatibility. An isomorphism of families carrying $K$ and the markings to each other identifies the marking ideals (also when it permutes the markings); the identical formula proves naturality. These are calculations with [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] and [def-pc-module-pullback], not an appeal to unspecified canonical maps.

proof.text: Fix a geometric fibre $Y/\Omega$ and a reduced component $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $Y$ is proper over $\Omega$, and so is its closed component $Z$. Properness includes finite type, so $Y$ is locally of finite presentation over the field $\Omega$, and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; it has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. The statement assumes the node condition only at nonsmooth closed points, while [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction] also requires every other point to be smooth; this is where reducedness enters. The algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is perfect, so for every field extension $k'/\Omega$ and every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$ (with $R$ reduced) the ring $R\otimes_\Omega k'$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor]. These rings cover $Y_{k'}$, so $Y$ is geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. By [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open] its smooth locus $W$ is a dense open. For an irreducible component $Z'$ with generic point $\eta$, the complement in $Y$ of the finitely many other components is a nonempty open contained in $Z'$. It meets $W$ in a point $y$. Since $\eta$ generizes $y$ and opens are stable under generization, $\eta\in W$. A non-closed point $y\in Y$ is such a generic point: its closure is irreducible, contains a closed point other than $y$, and lies in a component of dimension one. If the closure were smaller than that component, the closed point, the closure and the component would form a chain of length two. Hence every point of $Y$ other than its nonsmooth closed points is smooth, and $Y$ is pure of dimension one and of finite type over $\Omega$. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction]. That statement gives the finite normalization $C$, its proper smooth connected curve structure, the branch divisor $B_C$ (two branches for a self-node), and $\nu^*K_{Y/\Omega}\simeq\Omega^1_{C/\Omega}\otimes\mathcal O_C(B_C)$. Compose with the supplied identification $K|_Y\simeq K_{Y/\Omega}$. Every closed branch point is $\Omega$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], since $C$ is of finite type over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$.

proof.text: Each fibre marking is a distinct $\Omega$-point of the smooth locus of $Y$, with its reduced scheme structure. Near such a point $Y$ is a smooth curve and hence normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]; thus it has only one component there. Indeed its local ring is a domain, and the other finitely many components can be removed. The finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives the finite component set. Consequently $Z$ agrees with $Y$ near a marking on $Z$. The normalization-isomorphism clause of [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction] identifies its preimage with exactly one reduced $\Omega$-point on $C$, with the same local ideal. Away from these points the pulled-back marking ideal is the unit ideal. Therefore $\nu^*\mathcal O_Y(D_Y)\simeq\mathcal O_C(M_C)$: locally dualize the same single generator, as in step 4. Markings lie in the ambient smooth locus, whereas $B_C$ lies over the ambient singular locus, so their supports are disjoint. Each reduced point, and their finite sum $B_C+M_C$, is Cartier by [lem-sc-point-cartier].

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), and the normalization-isomorphism clause of lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction; marking pullback calculated on the smooth locus

proof.text: Restrict the comparison of step 3 to $Y$ and pull back to $C$. The tensor comparison [lem-pc-scheme-pullback-monoidal-existing] and steps 5--6 give $\nu^*(L|_Y)\simeq\Omega^1_{C/\Omega}\otimes\mathcal O_C(B_C)\otimes\mathcal O_C(M_C)$. Because the supports of $B_C$ and $M_C$ are disjoint, the product of their ideals is the ideal of their sum; locally at most one factor is nonunit. Dual frames consequently identify the last two factors with $\mathcal O_C(B_C+M_C)$, compatibly on overlaps. This is the asserted canonical isomorphism, relative to the given fibre identification of $K$.

source.place: Tags 01WT (definition-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors), 0C4U (lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors); tensor of dual ideal frames

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-differential-euler-degree] to the smooth proper connected $C/\Omega$: its differential line has Euler-characteristic degree $2g(C)-2$, and Euler-characteristic degree agrees with divisor/Picard degree for every invertible module. Apply the effective-divisor and rational-point clauses of [lem-pc-degree-base-change] to $B_C+M_C$. All its points are distinct and rational, with coefficient one, so its line has degree $\#B_C+\#M_C$; tensoring with the differential line adds that number to its degree. Step 7 therefore gives exactly $\deg\nu^*(L|_Y)=2g(C)-2+\#B_C+\#M_C$. The sum over no points is zero. With $n=0$ steps 2 and 6 give empty $D$ and $M_C$, without any positivity or stability assertion.
